rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Fungi are the absorptive kingdom: eukaryotic, chitin-walled, chlorophyll-less organisms whose mycelium of hyphae digests food externally and absorbs it, storing glycogen and reproducing by spores. Four classes separate by the sexual spore: phycomycetes (coenocytic, sporangiospores, zygospores — Mucor), ascomycetes (septate, conidia, ascospores inside an 8-spored ascus — yeast, Penicillium), basidiomycetes…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Fungal walls are chitin and the reserve is glycogen, which is why a mushroom is not given a place in Plantae even when it grows in soil like a plant.
Penicillium is an ascomycete used for penicillin. Puccinia, the wheat rust, is a basidiomycete even though it never looks like a mushroom. The sexual structure decides, not the shape of the colony.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Ascospore vs basidiospore:** ascospores form INSIDE a sac (ascus, usually 8); basidiospores form OUTSIDE on a club (basidium, usually 4). Endogenous vs exogenous is the one-line separator.  ·  **Hypha vs mycelium:** hypha = one filament; mycelium = the entire mass of hyphae.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 2024 asked fungi's general characteristics with one beneficial and one harmful example (2m) — a compact but exacting question: definition features + two named examples.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Rhizopus stolonifer*** — black bread mould; phycomycete; sporangiospores.  ·  ***Saccharomyces cerevisiae*** — baker's/brewer's yeast; ascomycete; budding.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is a mycelium? **Answer.** The **mass of hyphae** — branching filaments — that forms the body of a fungus. rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **External digestion:** fungi secrete hydrolytic enzymes into the substrate and absorb the digested products — the defining nutritional act of the kingdom.  ·  **Spore location as the classification key:** where the sexual spore is made (inside a sac vs outside a club vs unknown) separates the four classes.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Fungi: chitin wall, absorptive heterotrophs, glycogen reserve, mycelium of hyphae, spore reproduction, chief decomposers.  ·  Phycomycetes: coenocytic, sporangiospores, zygospores/oospores — Mucor, Phytophthora.  ·  Ascomycetes: septate, conidia, ascospores inside ascus (8), ascocarp — yeast, Penicillium.  ·  Basidiomycetes: septate dikaryotic, basidiospores outside basidium (4), basidiocarp, clamp connections — Agaricus, Puccinia, Ustilago.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Fleming discovered penicillin from Penicillium in 1928; mass production 1940s.  ·  Mycorrhiza ("fungus root") occurs in ~90% of plant families.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Kingdom of Absorbers Fungi are the kingdom of life that **eats by digesting outside its body**. A mushroom is only the fruiting body; the real fungus is a web of microscopic threads spreading through soil, bread or skin, pouring out enzymes and soaking back the products.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding — What Makes a Fungus a Fungus | Feature | Detail | Consequence | |---|---|---| | Cell wall | **Chitin** (fungal cellulose) + polysaccharides | Rigid, unlike cellulose walls of plants | | Nutrition | **Heterotrophic by absorption** — enzymes secreted onto food, products absorbed | External digestion; fungi live *inside their food* | |…  ·  ## 3. The Four Classes of Fungi — Classification by Reproduction Traditional classification separates fungi by **the type of sexual spore** (and mycelium type). Learn each class by: mycelium → asexual spore → sexual spore → examples.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Deuteromycetes: sexual stage unknown, conidia — Penicillium, Alternaria, Fusarium.  ·  Economic: yeast (bread/alcohol), Penicillium (penicillin), Agaricus (food), mycorrhiza (agriculture) vs Puccinia/Ustilago (crops), Aspergillus (spoilage), Candida (thrush), Amanita (poison).  ·  **Deuteromycetes are not a natural class:** they are a temporary holding group of fungi whose sexual phase is unknown — mostly ascomycetes in reality.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Yeast is unicellular but still a fungus:** it is an ascomycete; unicellularity does not disqualify it.  ·  **Coenocytic vs septate:** coenocytic = one continuous tube with many nuclei (phycomycetes); septate = divided by cross-walls with pores (ascomycetes, basidiomycetes).  ·  ***Puccinia graminis*** — wheat rust; basidiomycete; alternating hosts (wheat + barberry).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ***Phytophthora infestans*** — late blight of potato; caused the Irish famine (1845).  ·  "Classify the four classes with spore type" is the core exam skill — build the four-column table from memory.  ·  "A fungus lives inside its own food."

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why can't fungi live without moisture even though they grow on dry-looking bread? **Answer.** Every active stage of a fungus is **a wall of water**: absorption — its only way of feeding — works by digesting food externally and drawing the dissolved nutrients **through the wall by osmosis**, which requires a film of…  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  **Deep dive — reading the class from the spore.** The fastest exam skill in mycology: name the sexual spore and you have named the class. Zygospore → Phycomycetes. Ascospore in an ascus → Ascomycetes. Basidiospore on a basidium → Basidiomycetes. No known sexual stage → Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi).…
